keywords.primary: how to raise prices in your HVAC business

instagram.caption:
How to raise prices in your HVAC, plumbing, electrical or roofing business, and tell customers why.
Jobber's 2026 Home Service Trends Report (survey of 1,050 US home service business owners, December 2025): 65% raised prices last year. HVAC 83%; plumbing, electrical and roofing 74% each; cleaning 55%, the lowest.
The reasons they named: inflation 72%, labor costs 50%.
Federal data (BLS Employment Cost Index, 12 months to June 2026): wages for installation, maintenance and repair workers rose 3.7%; all civilian workers 3.2%.

Pricing Clinic, Lesson 6. Send this before your next quote (example):
"Starting [date], our rates go up."
"Our labor and material costs rose this year."
"Anything you've already approved stays at the price we quoted."

Keep that last line: raise the next job, never one already approved.
One honest note: Jobber sells software, and its survey shows who raised prices, not how customers took it. Watch your close rate for a month after.

Send this to whoever writes your quotes.

youtube.title: How to Raise Prices in Your HVAC Business (Plumbing, Electrical, Roofing Too)
youtube.description:
How to raise prices in your HVAC business, and the note that tells customers why.
For HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing and home service business owners.
Jobber, "Blue Collar Strong: The 2026 Home Service Trends Report": a survey of 1,050 US home service business owners, conducted through Conjointly in December 2025. 65% raised prices last year; by trade, HVAC 83%, plumbing 74%, electrical 74%, roofing 74%, cleaning 55%. Most common reasons: inflation (72%) and labor costs (50%). Jobber sells field service software. https://www.getjobber.com/home-service-trends-report/
US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Cost Index, June 2026 (released Jul 31, 2026), wages and salaries, civilian workers, 12 months ending June 2026: installation, maintenance, and repair 3.7%; all workers 3.2%. https://www.bls.gov/news.release/eci.htm

The price note (example):
1. "Starting [date], our rates go up."
2. "Our labor and material costs rose this year."
3. "Anything you've already approved stays at the price we quoted."
Raise the next job, never one already approved. The survey shows who raised prices, not how customers took it: watch your close rate for a month after.

Send this to whoever writes your quotes.
